newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: FOCUS - Nestle shares dip despite sales rise.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Nestle shares dip despite sales rise.

text.p: Nestle SA said first-half sales rose 17.5 percent to 33.5 billion Swiss francs ($22.6 billion), helped by favourable currency rates and rising volume growth.

But its shares dipped on Wednesday because investors had expected even stronger volume growth. Analysts said the shares could remain under pressure for a few days before regaining momentum on good longer-term growth prospects.
"The favourable foreign exchange rates contributed nearly 11 percent to the increase in consolidated sales," the world's biggest food company said from its Vevey headquarters.
"Real internal growth, not including acquisitions and divestments, stands at 2.7 percent, while it amounted to only 2.2 percent during the first three months of the year," it said.
Internal growth rates were particularly high in North America and in Eastern Europe, as well as in the Middle East and in Southeast Asian countries, it said in a statement.
It cited significant progress in pet care products, in its mineral water division and by its Alcon pharmaceuticals unit.
"Coffee also showed positive volume growth, in spite of the price increases made necessary as a result of the rise in green coffee prices," it said.
It gave no other details on sales or profits.
The 17.5 percent rise was down from the 18.7 percent growth rate in the first quarter, reflecting in part slightly less favourable Swiss franc exchange rates.

"For 1997 as a whole, the Nestle group remains confident that the favourable rate of internal growth will continue. Consolidated sales should therefore also grow, albeit at a slower rate than during the first half of 1997 as a result of the expected foreign exchange evolution," it said.
"As for consolidated net profit, Nestle expects it to evolve in line with consolidated sales." Nestle made a 1996 net profit of 3.40 billion francs on 60.49 billion in sales.
Nestle shares opened four Swiss francs weaker at 1,965 francs and touched a low at 1,940 before rebounding, only to turn lower again. They were off nine francs at 1,960 around 0940 GMT.

"Volume growth was significantly weaker than what I was forecasting and also a little bit weaker than consensus," James Amoroso at Bank Julius Baer said. "I am a little concerned about volume growth. It is not clear where the problem was," he said.
"I would advise caution over the coming days, but I think once the dust has cleared I think people will realise Nestle is still undervalued relative to the market."
Nestle shares have lagged the blue-chip Swiss Market Index by around nine percent over the past six months
Anne Alexandre at CSFB in London said the sales figure of 33.5 billion was just below her forecast of 33.8 billion. She had been looking for 3.1 percent volume growth.

"But I am not too concerned because it still means that the second quarter saw volume growth of three percent compared with 2.2 percent in the first quarter," she said, and this despite poor weather in June and the effect of coffee price hikes.
She said Nestle would struggle to hit its target of four percent volume growth this year.
"I think the four percent (target) depended on summer weather. They were expecting a rebound compared with bad summer weather last year."

Any more coffee price rises could weigh on volume by curtailing consumer demand, she said, noting the biggest risk Nestle faced was that frost could hurt Brazil's coffee crop and drive prices higher at a time of low stocks.

"Overall I have a buy recommendation. I still like the stock. I think that if they can achieve close to 3.5 percent (volume growth) for the full year it is still a very good achievement compared with what they have been able to achieve in past years," she said.

"They are positioned in such a way that they have growth in emerging markets even if there are slowdowns in some parts. That I like, and on top of that they are doing the right thing in their traditional markets-- cost cutting."
She suggested buying on the dips.
Amoroso said he was not concerned about coffee sales.
"Coffee is fine and coffee is the single most important factor in Nestle operating profit. So that is the good news, but they must have a problem somewhere else."
($ = 1.481 Swiss Francs)
